samples.summary: The CLI half of the nonce feature — sending `cliState` in the OAuth URL — has no test at all
samples.evidence: The whole security property depends on `login`'s action appending `&cliState=${encodeURIComponent(state)}` (login.ts:71-73) and passing the same `state` to `startCallbackServer` (login.ts:58-64). The new suite `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts` only imports `startCallbackServer`/`stateMatches`/`UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` and calls them directly with a nonce it mints itself; nothing imports `registerLoginCommand` or runs the action. If the `&cliState=` term were dropped (or the nonce passed to the server differed from the one in the URL), every test in the diff — CLI and backend — would still pass, while every real login would 400 with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE.

samples.summary: `--allow-unbound-callback` flag wiring is untested; only the internal `allowUnbound` option is exercised
samples.evidence: login-callback.test.ts:104/115 call `startCallbackServer(NONCE, { allowUnbound: true })` directly. Nothing asserts that commander's `--allow-unbound-callback` maps to `localOpts.allowUnboundCallback` and thence to `allowUnbound` (login.ts:17-21, 62). A rename/typo in the option name would leave the flag silently inert with a green suite.

samples.summary: No test that the nonce is kept out of the stderr banner (the stated reason for splitting the printed URL from `oauthUrl`)
samples.evidence: login.ts:66-76 deliberately prints a nonce-free URL to stderr and only prints the full URL in the browser-open failure path. No test observes `console.error` from the login action (no test imports the command at all), so a regression that logs `oauthUrl` unconditionally — reintroducing the nonce into scrollback/CI logs — is invisible.

samples.summary: The nonce-less branch of the redirect (`state.cliState` falsy → no `&state=`) is not distinguished by any test
samples.evidence: The new controller test (auth.controller.spec.ts:218-235) covers the nonce present case with an end-anchored regex. The pre-existing test at spec.ts:205-209 uses an UNANCHORED regex `/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/`, which matches whether or not a `&state=` is appended, so nothing pins the `''` branch of `state.cliState ? ... : ''`. Also, `encodeURIComponent(state.cliState)` is only exercised with `'nonce-abc'`, which needs no escaping.

samples.summary: No test for a malformed `cliState` arriving with an invalid/absent port — `normalizeCliState` is never reached, so the documented "never a silent drop" guarantee has a hole with no coverage
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.ts:66-75 only calls `normalizeCliState` inside the `Number.isInteger(portNum) && 1024..65535` branch. github-auth.guard.spec.ts only exercises `port: '49152'` (valid) or the web flow (no mode). A request `?mode=cli&port=80&cliState=nope` silently proceeds with no 400 and no state token, and no test covers that combination.

mergedFrom.summary: No test that the nonce is kept out of the stderr banner (the stated reason for splitting the printed URL from `oauthUrl`)
mergedFrom.evidence: login.ts:66-76 deliberately prints a nonce-free URL to stderr and only prints the full URL in the browser-open failure path. No test observes `console.error` from the login action (no test imports the command at all), so a regression that logs `oauthUrl` unconditionally — reintroducing the nonce into scrollback/CI logs — is invisible.

verdict.reason: The CLI-side half of the nonce binding is genuinely untested. login.ts:58-73 mints `state`, hands it to `startCallbackServer(state, …)`, and appends `&cliState=${encodeURIComponent(state)}` to the OAuth URL; nothing asserts that these two values are the same, or that the `cliState` term is emitted at all. The only new suite, packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts, imports just `UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE`/`startCallbackServer`/`stateMatches` (lines 3-7) and drives the server with a nonce it mints itself (line 9), so it cannot fail if the URL term is dropped or a different nonce is put in the URL. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide greps for `cliState` (only login.ts, backend sources/spec, docs), `mode=cli`, `registerLoginCommand`, `allowUnbound`, `auth/github`, `startCallbackServer`, `vi.mock('open')`, `oauthUrl`/`Opening browser`/`buildLoginUrl`; no e2e/integration directories; the command-wiring suite namespaces.test.ts:11-20 never registers the login command; bin.test.ts mocks src/cli.js wholesale. The one backend spec hit (github-auth.guard.spec.ts) covers the server's parsing of cliState, not the CLI's emission of it. Major under the missing-tests rubric: a security-relevant behavior change with no meaningful test.

finding.summary: The CLI-side nonce check — the central new behavior of this delta — has no test at all
finding.evidence: `startCallbackServer`/`stateMatches` in packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:168-214 add the guard that rejects a `/callback?code=…` lacking this invocation's nonce (400 'State mismatch', without settling the promise). Nothing exercises it: neither helper is exported, `registerLoginCommand` is only wired in packages/cli/src/cli.ts, and no file under packages/cli/test references login, /callback, state matching or 'State mismatch'. The only tests added in this delta are packages/cli/test/url.test.ts (about `seg`) and one backend controller test for the redirect. So the CLI could stop enforcing the nonce (e.g. accept a null state, or compare the wrong field) and the green suite would say nothing — this is precisely the fake-coverage shape: the security fix is described in comments and asserted only on the backend half.

verdict.reason: The finding's factual premises are false. Both helpers ARE exported (login.ts:200 `export function stateMatches`, login.ts:222 `export function startCallbackServer`), and a dedicated test file exists at packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts that imports them directly (lines 3-7) and exercises the nonce guard end-to-end against a real HTTP server with real fetch calls — no over-mocking. Specifically: lines 32-41 unit-test the constant-time comparison including `stateMatches(NONCE, null) === false` (line 39, exactly the "accept a null state" mutation the reviewer claimed would go undetected) and off-by-one/length variants; lines 59-82 assert the wrong-nonce callback yields 400 'State mismatch' (lines 66-67), does NOT settle the promise (line 71), and that the real callback still wins afterward (lines 73-78) — directly covering the guard at login.ts:276-280; lines 84-101 cover the nonce-less/version-skew path (login.ts:263-271); lines 103-124 cover both --allow-unbound-callback branches including that a wrong nonce is still refused; lines 126-141 cover missing-code and unknown-path without settling. The file is genuinely executed: vitest.config.ts:5 includes 'test/**/*.test.ts' and package.json:19 runs 'vitest --run', with no exclusion. The claimed failure mode (weakening or removing the nonce check would leave the suite green) is contradicted by lines 39 and 66-71, which would fail.

finding.summary: New CLI_STATE_PATTERN validation in GitHubAuthGuard is untested — no guard spec exists
finding.evidence: This delta adds `CLI_STATE_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/` and the `typeof cliState === 'string' && test(...) ? cliState : undefined` branch (github-auth.guard.ts:18, 31-38). There is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts`: `packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts` contains only auth.controller, jwt.strategy, github.strategy, cli-auth.store and auth.service specs. So neither the accept path (a real 43-char base64url nonce stored on the state), the reject path (malformed/array/absent cliState → stored as undefined), nor the boundary lengths are covered. A pattern that silently rejected the CLI's real nonce format would ship green and break every `wafflebase login` with 'State mismatch'.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` exists and that the CLI_STATE_PATTERN accept path, reject path, and boundary lengths are untested. The file exists at packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.spec.ts and is collected by jest (packages/backend/package.json:106-107, rootDir "src" + testRegex ".*\\.spec\\.ts$"). It covers: the accept path with a real 43-char base64url nonce from randomBytes(32) (spec:19-24), the absent path returning undefined (spec:26-28), boundary lengths 'abc' (<16) and 'a'.repeat(129) (>128) (spec:43-44), non-string/array/empty/charset rejections (spec:42-51), and duplicate-array conflict (spec:35-40). Guard-level tests use a real CliAuthStore and assert the nonce is actually persisted and readable back via consumeState (spec:60-63, 79-98), with 400 paths asserting createState was never called (spec:100-121) — so it is neither absent nor over-mocked. The finding's quoted code is also inaccurate: the guard throws BadRequestException rather than silently coercing to undefined (github-auth.guard.ts:25-41).
